scope: Standing main royal palace (Haw Kham), now the Luang Prabang National Museum. Includes the mapped reception, throne and residential building wings, the front marble steps and the Lao gilded spire.

rejectedWideCrop.reason: Invalid river-edge values outside the area used for the palace review.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: The museum identifies the palace completed in 1909, its conversion to the current National Museum and its standing historic rooms.
The municipal tourism authority describes the Lao and French Beaux-Arts design and later Lao replacement of the spire above the throne chamber.
The heritage interpretation plan inventories the former palace and Haw Phabang separately.

limitations: The native polygon controls the exterior footprint and its orientation. Small porch projections, roof and wall heights, rear window arrangement and small roof ornament need interpretation.
The bowed gable trim, royal emblem and gilded pinnacle will be modeled at exterior-view scale from the verified Qualla photo, with simplified ornamental relief.
The terrain review uses a 160 m crop from the original tile. A wider crop crossed invalid river-edge values outside the palace site. The palace threshold elevation is estimated.
next: Build the crossed palace wings, broad raised stairs, dark tiered roofs and gold Lao throne-hall pinnacle.

sectionDatum.basis: Estimated raised level floor above the unmodified site elevation. Front stairs meet the south approach.
